summary: The prepared base already contains the upstream ROCm fix: HIP uses Triton top-k/top-p renormalizers and the DSPARK probability builder has safe PyTorch fallbacks when optional functions are unavailable. Added issue-specific regression coverage; no production source change was justified.

tests.what_was_measured: Two GPU tests passed: live ROCm Triton top-k/top-p renormalization matched explicit expected distributions, and the DSPARK target-probability builder matched an independent PyTorch reference when both optional renormalizer globals were forced to None. Boundaries included top-k 1, 3, and above vocabulary size plus top-p 0.55, 0.8, and 1.0.

tests.command: pre-commit run ruff-format --files test/registered/spec/dspark/test_dspark_sampling_renorm.py && pre-commit run ruff --files test/registered/spec/dspark/test_dspark_sampling_renorm.py
tests.what_was_measured: The new regression test passed repository formatting and lint checks.

gpu_execution.evidence: Executed with ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 on the sole assigned AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2.26015. Raw pytest output is retained at reports/j-1887d0f26a67/raw/pytest_dspark_sampling_renorm.log.

remaining_limitations: Kimi-K3 and RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark weights were unavailable. Only one MI355X was assigned, not the reported eight-MI350X TP8 system. Full-model startup, request transport, semantic accuracy, five-minute serving behavior, and distributed execution were not reproduced. No native code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
